name: shared
extends: tools/microbench/shared/protocol-v2.json (its leaves stay installed; this version adds the store step of a round: who is held by a shared store, and how many warps are accepted at once)
mechanisms: synchronization.cta.release (only as the tail the stores are read against)
data_seen_before_writing: tma_store_loaded store_round r3 binaries, fg-gemm/epilogue-replay/hw-extra-{b300,h100}: round = [4 x STS.128 by W warps (64 B lane stride = 16 wavefronts per store), bar.sync, bar.sync]; periods for W = 0..4 without clock reads 66.8 / 132.6 / 141.1 / 203.7 / 262.3 (b300) and 65.3 / 131.3 / 141.1 / 203.8 / 262.3 (h100); the same with fence.proxy.async before the barriers 95.8 / 213.0 / 222.5 / 287.3 / 354.0 and 94.0 / 211.0 / 217.5 / 286.3 / 349.0; and the stamped (clock-read) timelines of the same cells. Engine replay of the W = 4 cells (fg-gemm/epilogue-replay/fence-{b300,h100}): 253.5 / 253.9 without the fence. No cell of this protocol has been run.
why_the_seen_data_does_not_settle_it: Three readings fit the five periods: (a) the stores hold their warps and W warps cost 1 / 1.13 / 2.08 / 2.97 units of 65.8 cycles (two warps accepted at once, further warps serial); (b) one acceptance server at ~16.4 cycles per store (W x 65.6 = 131 / 197 / 262 for W = 2..4, the barrier pair overlapping the drain) plus something that makes a lone writer pay 65.8 + 66.8; (c) a bound on outstanding stores per warp. The stamped timelines cannot separate them: BAR.SYNC.DEFER_BLOCKING lets the clock read behind it issue before the barrier holds the warp (non-writers' stamp C precedes the writers' stamp B), on b300 a lone writer's clock read after its four stores comes 12.8 cycles late and the round grows by 9.7 only, on h100 the same cell delays every warp's clock read by 48 cycles. The clock reads themselves hide or move the wait.
question: (1) What does a shared store hold: the issuing warp until the store is accepted, only a later barrier / fence of that warp, or nothing until a bound on outstanding stores is reached? (2) How many warps' stores does one SM accept at a time, and which warps exclude each other? (3) Does the answer change with the wavefront count of a store or with the banks consecutive stores touch?
probe: tools/microbench/shared/probe/store_step.cu (header comment = round shapes). One CTA of 4 warps on one SM; round = [K stores by the warps of a 4-bit mask] TAIL, no clock read inside the round, one clock64 before and after each warp's loop, per-warp period = cycles / rounds. TAIL 0 nothing, 1 bar.sync, 2 bar.sync x 2, 3 FILL, 4 FILL + bar.sync x 2, 5 bar.sync x 2 + FILL, 6 fence.proxy.async.shared::cta + bar.sync x 2. FILL = NFILL dependent mad.lo.u32 carried from round to round. 2048 rounds, 8 launches after a discarded one, runs a and b.

geometry.G16: st.shared.v4.b32, lane stride 64 B, store step 16 B, same banks in every warp: 16 wavefronts per store, the K stores of a thread on disjoint banks (the store_round / GEMM epilogue pattern)
geometry.G16same: the same with store step 512 B: the K stores of a thread on the same banks
geometry.G16shift: G16 with warp w shifted by 16 w bytes: warps issuing the same store index touch disjoint banks
geometry.G4: st.shared.v4.b32, lane stride 16 B, store step 512 B: 4 wavefronts per store
geometry.N1: st.shared.b32, lane stride 4 B, store step 128 B: 1 wavefront per store
geometry.N16: st.shared.b32, lane stride 64 B, store step 4 B: 16 wavefronts per store
geometry.N32: st.shared.b32, lane stride 128 B, store step 4 B: 32 wavefronts per store

cells: run_store_step.sh (222 cells per run). A: TAIL 0, G16, K = 4 for the 15 non-empty masks, K in {1, 2, 8} for masks {1, 3, 15}. B: TAIL 3, G16, NFILL in {8, 24, 64} x K in {1, 2, 4, 8} x masks {0, 1, 3, 15}. C: TAIL 2, G16, K = 4 for all 16 masks, K in {1, 2, 8} for masks {0, 1, 3, 15}; TAIL 1, G16, K = 4 masks {0, 1, 3, 7, 15}, K in {1, 2, 8} masks {0, 1, 15}. D: TAIL 4 and 5, G16, K = 4, NFILL in {24, 64}, masks {0, 1, 3, 15}. E: the six other geometries, K = 4 (N1: K = 8), TAIL 0 masks {1, 3, 15} and TAIL 2 masks {0, 1, 3, 15}. F: TAIL 6, G16, K in {1, 2, 4, 8} x masks {0, 1, 3, 15}. G (added before any run, see addenda): G4, TAIL 6, K in {1, 2, 4, 8} x masks {0, 1, 3, 15}; G4, TAIL 2, K in {1, 2, 8} x masks {0, 1, 3, 15}; G4, TAIL 3, NFILL 24, K in {4, 8} x masks {0, 1, 15}.
sass_gate: sass_check_store_step.py (run by build_store_step.sh, failure stops the run): for each of the 36 k_step<WIDE, K, TAIL, NFILL> instantiations the loop (the body between the target of the backward branch that closes the round and that branch) contains exactly K STS (STS.128 for WIDE 1, a 32-bit STS for WIDE 0), the tail's BAR.SYNC 0x1, 0x80 count (0 / 1 / 2), exactly NFILL IMAD for tails 3 / 4 / 5 and none otherwise, one MEMBAR + one FENCE.VIEW.ASYNC for tail 6 and none otherwise, no CS2R / S2R, and no load; the script prints each loop and whether the stores are predicated (@P STS) or branched over, and the loop length. A loop duplicated by the compiler (2K stores) fails the gate.

derivation.units: u(geometry) = P(TAIL 0, mask 1, K) / K, the cycles one store of that geometry costs a lone free-running warp (its acceptance at full rate). c_n(K) = P(TAIL 3, mask 0, K, NFILL n), b2 = P(TAIL 2, mask 0), b1 = P(TAIL 1, mask 0).
derivation.hold: H(K, n) = P(TAIL 3, mask 1, K, n) - c_n(K), warp 0's period (the writer).
derivation.bystander: Y(K, n) = P(TAIL 3, mask 1, K, n) - c_n(K) read on warps 1-3 (non-writers of the same cell): what a store costs warps that do not write.
derivation.barrier: Bd(mask, K) = P(TAIL 2, mask, K) - b2; ordering cells T4(mask, n) = P(TAIL 4, mask, n) - P(TAIL 4, 0, n), T5 likewise.
derivation.concurrency: R(mask) = P(TAIL 0, mask, K = 4) of each writing warp / (4 u): 1 = that warp is accepted as if alone, popcount(mask) = fully serial.
derivation.fence: Df(mask, K) = P(TAIL 6, mask, K) - P(TAIL 2, mask, K); written bytes = popcount(mask) x K x 512.

hypotheses_declared_before_data.hold_HB_issue: a shared store holds its warp's next issue until the store is accepted: H(K, n) = K u within max(15 %, 6 cycles) for every n, T4 = T5 = Bd.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.hold_HG_background: stores drain behind the warp: H(K, n) <= 4.5 K + 6 cycles whenever c_n >= K u; then Bd comes from the barrier and T4(mask 1, n = 64) is smaller than Bd by at least half of min(K u, c_64) while T5 = Bd.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.hold_HD_bounded: at most d stores of a warp outstanding: H(K, n) = max(0, K - d) u for c_n >= d u, one d in {1, 2, 3} for every K and both n = 24 and 64.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.bystander: Y = 0 within 6 cycles (stores of one warp do not stall the other warps); if Y exceeds 6 cycles on both runs it is recorded as an SM-wide stall and enters the rule.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.concurrency_S1_single: R(mask) = popcount(mask) within 10 % for all 15 masks: one acceptance server per SM, and the W = 2..4 periods already seen are that server's throughput with the barrier pair overlapping the drain.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.concurrency_S2_pairs: the six two-warp masks split into parallel (R <= 1.25) and serial (R >= 1.7) pairs consistent with two servers, each owning a fixed set of warps; the three- and four-warp masks then follow from the two sets within 10 %.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.concurrency_S3_first_two: every two-warp mask is parallel (R <= 1.25), three warps cost 2 units and four warps 3 (R = 2.0 +- 0.25, 3.0 +- 0.3): two stores are accepted at a time only while no third warp competes.
hypotheses_declared_before_data.wavefronts: u(G4) / u(G16) = 4 / 16 and u(N16) / u(N32) = 16 / 32 within 15 %, u(N1) = the installed STS issue interval within 15 % (b300 4.388, h100 4.415); u(G16same) = u(G16shift) = u(G16) within 10 % (the banks of consecutive stores and of other warps do not matter). A geometry that breaks this is recorded and the rule is installed only for what the cells cover.

decision: Exactly one hold hypothesis and one concurrency hypothesis must hold on both runs of a device for that device to get a rule; the choice is read from the TAIL 0 / TAIL 3 cells first (no barrier involved) and then checked on TAIL 1 / 2 / 4 / 5: a closed-form model built from the chosen pair, u, c_n, b1 and b2 only (model_store_step.py, written after the decision, no fitted parameter) must reproduce every A-D cell within max(10 %, 8 cycles). If no pair holds, or the model misses more than 1 cell in 10, nothing is installed and the misses are listed for the next version.

rule_forms.HB: engine: a synchronous shared store sets its warp's control floor to its acceptance end (the per-SM acceptance frontier it already books).
rule_forms.HG: engine: BAR.SYNC and proxy fence of a warp start no earlier than the acceptance end of that warp's own earlier shared stores; the warp itself is not held.
rule_forms.HD: engine: a warp may have d accepted-but-undrained shared stores; the d+1-th waits for the oldest. New timing_row field (ids 20-29) outstanding_stores on storage.shared.acceptance_sm, value d, measured.
rule_forms.S1: no change to the per-SM acceptance frontier.
rule_forms.S2_S3: the per-SM acceptance frontier becomes the measured set of servers (S2: one frontier per warp set, keyed by the SMSP sets the masks identify; S3: two frontiers, a store takes the earlier one, with the measured cost of a third competitor). New timing_row field on storage.shared.acceptance_sm carrying the server count; value from the mask cells, measured when runs agree within 3 %.

fence_prediction_check: Df(mask, K) for the 12 dirty cells against the installed storage.shared.fence leaf (b300 75.26 + bytes / 569.0, h100 74.51 + bytes / 751.8) and Df(0, K) against the clean fence 29.0 / 28.75: a check within 8 cycles confirms the leaf (bytes 512 .. 16384 instead of the 2048 .. 8192 it was derived from). Outside: reported; the leaf is re-derived by ordinary least squares over these 12 cells per device (new hardware data, experimental) only if the residuals of that fit are at most 6 cycles.

acceptance.C1: TAIL 2, G16, K = 4, masks 0 / 1 / 3 / 7 / 15 within 5 % of the store_round periods above (W = 0..4).
acceptance.C2: TAIL 6, G16, K = 4, masks 0 / 1 / 15 within 5 % of the store_round fence periods (W = 0, 1, 4).
acceptance.C3: runs a and b within 3 % per cell and warp.
acceptance.note: store_round's loop is unrolled four times and rotates over four boxes; this probe's is not. A control miss that is the same offset (within 3 cycles) in every mask of a tail is a loop-overhead difference: the differences H, Bd, T4, T5, Df are read against this probe's own mask-0 cells and stay valid; any other control miss voids the cells of that tail.

install: Engine rule in the selected form(s); storage.shared.acceptance_sm / issue values unchanged unless the wavefronts check fails by more than 15 % with runs agreeing (then the per-wavefront value of the failing class is re-derived from u, measured). Source keys shared.<device>.store_step, artifact fg-line-sync/store-step/<device>-<run>/. Validation: the tracer captures of fg-gemm/epilogue-replay/cap-{b300,h100} replayed (sts, fence, full cells against hardware), CTest, pytest, cyclescope tree build && cyclescope tree validate --strict, full-gpu and single-cluster 500 x 2.
not_allowed: no case-cycle tuning; no values from other machines; no use of full-gpu error to choose a hypothesis or a value; no hypothesis added after data without an addendum that says the data was seen.

addenda.text: Cells G added before the first run. Reason (read from existing data, no cell of this protocol seen): the store addresses of the captured block-scaled DSL GEMM epilogue (CUF-DSL-BS-NVF4-V16-R05, SASS 0x1c40-0x1f70) are swizzled within each 64 B row, so one STS.128 there is 4 wavefronts, not the 16 of store_round's unswizzled pattern; the fence and hold questions must therefore also be answered at 4 wavefronts per store. The fence prediction check is extended to these 12 dirty G4 cells with the same bytes rule (bytes = popcount x K x 512); if the G16 and G4 cells of equal bytes differ by more than 8 cycles the fence cost is not a function of bytes alone: both tables are reported, the candidate axes fixed here are written bytes, written wavefronts and store count, and the leaf is re-derived only if one of them fits all 24 dirty cells within 6 cycles.

addenda.after_run: store-step b300-r1 (GPU-ca40cb09) and h100-r1 (GPU-e76c5c58), 222 cells x 2 runs each, SASS gate 36 / 36, runs a / b within 0.3 %
addenda.written: after seeing the data; everything below that is not a declared check is marked as such
addenda.controls: C3 holds. C2 (fence round, masks 0 / 1 / 15): 106.0 / 225.0 / 366.0 (b300) and 106.0 / 225.0 / 363.0 (h100) against 95.8 / 213.0 / 354.0 and 94.0 / 211.0 / 349.0: +10.2 / +12.0 / +12.0 and +12.0 / +14.0 / +14.0 cycles, the common loop offset the note allows (this loop is 24-26 instructions with nine register moves; store_round's is shorter). C1 (barrier round, masks 0 / 1 / 3 / 7 / 15): 76.0 / 131.6 / 140.0 / 201.9 / 259.9 and 76.0 / 130.4 / 140.0 / 202.0 / 260.0 against 66.8 / 132.6 / 141.1 / 203.7 / 262.3 and 65.3 / 131.3 / 141.1 / 203.8 / 262.3: masks 1-15 within 1 %, mask 0 +13.8 % / +16.4 %. By the letter C1 fails on mask 0 and the miss is not a common offset. It is kept as a failed control and the tail is still read, for a reason seen in the data: the writing rounds are bound by the store pipe, not by the loop, so the loop's own length shows only in the round without stores; nothing below uses P(TAIL 2, mask 0) except as the floor of max().
addenda.declared_hypotheses: hold: HB rejected (H(K, n) = 1.0-5.0 cycles where it predicts K u = 32-256); HD rejected (same cells); HG's first clause holds (stores drain behind the warp, FILL of another register chain overlaps them completely: P(TAIL 3, mask 1, K = 4, n = 64) = 268.1 / 264.0 against c_n = 263.1 / 263.0) but its barrier clause fails: T5 = T4 = 0 (the barrier pair does not wait for the stores either). bystander: 0 for warps running FILL once c_n covers the acceptance; warps whose loop holds predicated-off stores are delayed (TAIL 0 mask 1: 64-79 against 38 with nobody writing): a predicated-off STS still takes its turn behind stores in flight; recorded, not modelled. concurrency: with u = 32 none of S1 / S2 / S3 holds (R = 1.06 for every two-warp mask, 1.53 for three, 2.00 for four). wavefronts: u(N16) / u(N32) = 0.500, u(G16same) = u(G16shift) = u(G16) to 0.01 cycle (banks of consecutive stores and of other warps do not matter), u(N1) = 4.88 / 5.01 against the issue interval 4.388 / 4.415 (+11 % / +13 %, inside 15 %); u(G4) / u(G16) = 0.40 / 0.48 against 0.25: fails. By the decision rule as written nothing would be installed.
addenda.what_the_data_shows: u was assumed to be the per-SM cost (about 16.4 cycles per 16-wavefront store). The cells give two rates, the same on both devices: a lone warp is accepted at 2.00 cycles per wavefront (G16 / N16 31.98, N32 63.87 per store, K = 1..8), the SM as a whole at 1.00 (four warps: 16.00 / 31.97 per store). Two warps cost 34.0 each, three 49.0. Nothing holds the issuing warp and no barrier waits: every period of tails 1-5 is max(period without stores, store-pipe period).
addenda.model_check_written_after_data: fg-line-sync/tools/model_store_step.py, no fitted parameter: u1 = P(TAIL 0, mask 1, K = 4) / 4, u4 = P(TAIL 0, mask 15, K = 4) / 16, S(mask, K) = max(K u1, popcount K u4), P(tail, mask, K, n) = max(P(tail, 0, K, n), S). All 82 G16 cells of tails 1-5 on each device are inside max(10 %, 8 cycles) (mean absolute 4.8 / 4.3 cycles, largest +26.5 / +20.5 on a 282 / 276 cycle cell). Residual: two writers 136 (model 128, +6 %), three 196 (192).
addenda.decision_and_why_the_written_rule_is_rel: The written rule (one declared hold and one declared concurrency hypothesis) is not met; the misses above stay on record. A rule is installed nevertheless because the two-rate reading has no free parameter, both rates are read from single cells (TAIL 0, masks 1 and 15), it reproduces every other cell, and it is checked on data that did not shape it: the tracer captures of store_round (fg-gemm/epilogue-replay/cap-{b300,h100}: sts, fence, full cells) and new captures of store_step cells are replayed through the engine before any full-gpu run. Full-gpu error is not used to choose anything.
addenda.rule: New mechanism storage.shared.acceptance_smsp (timing kind 80, STS and the generic ST alias, own-CTA shared memory): a store occupies its SMSP's acceptance for cycles(shared_wavefronts); stores of one SMSP are accepted one after another; the store completes, and a later proxy fence of its CTA starts, no earlier than that; the issuing warp is not held. The per-SM frontier (storage.shared.acceptance_sm) and the per-SMSP issue interval (storage.shared.issue) are unchanged. Assumption, not measured here: the unit is the SMSP (the probe has one warp per SMSP), as for storage.shared.issue.
addenda.leaf: cycles = linear(shared_wavefronts), knots 1 / 4 / 16 / 32. 16 and 32: u(G16) = 31.98, u(N32) = 63.87 on both devices, measured. 1: the installed issue interval (4.388 b300, 4.415 h100), which N1 confirms within 15 %. 4: the declared u(G4) = P(TAIL 0, mask 1) / 4 gives 12.76 (b300) and 15.51 (h100); the h100 value contradicts its own K = 8 cell (P(TAIL 2, G4, mask 1, K = 8) = 110.0 < 8 x 15.51), so that loop is not bound by the store pipe there. Derivation fixed after data for both devices: u(G4) = (P(TAIL 2, G4, mask 1, K = 8) - [P(TAIL 2, G16, mask 1, K = 8) - 8 u(G16)]) / 8 = (107.0 - 5.0) / 8 = 12.75 (b300, equal to the declared value, measured) and (110.0 - 6.0) / 8 = 13.0 (h100, experimental; other readings of the same device 11.7-14.8). Wavefront counts 2-3 and 5-15 are interpolated, not measured.
addenda.not_changed: storage.shared.acceptance_sm: at 4 wavefronts four warps cost 4.72 (b300) / 4.45 (h100) per store against the leaf's 4.01 / 4.04 (+18 % / +10 %; 16.00 and 31.97 at 16 and 32 wavefronts agree). The install clause would re-derive the b300 value; it is left as is and listed, because the cells cannot see that leaf at one wavefront (the SMSP rate binds) and turning an installed slope into a knot table belongs with a run that covers 1-8 wavefronts.
addenda.fence: Prediction check as declared: fails. Df against the installed leaf (76-104 at these bytes): G16 65 / 83 / 93 / 99 (mask 1, K = 1..8), 69 / 88 / 94 / 95 (mask 3), 99 / 96 / 106 / 113 (mask 15) on b300, the same within 4 on h100; G4 42-102. G16 and G4 cells of equal bytes differ by up to 44 cycles and ordinary least squares over bytes leaves residuals of 17.7 / 18.1 (G16) and 20.7 / 13.8 (G4): by the declared rule the leaf is not re-derived from Df. Reason (seen in the data): Df, like the D(W) the leaf was derived from, subtracts a barrier round in which the barriers overlap the acceptance; in the fence round they cannot, so the difference is mostly the lost overlap (60-76 cycles), not a drain. Derivation fixed after data: with A = P(TAIL 0, mask, K) (the measured acceptance period of the same stores) the dirty round exceeds the clean one by A + w; w = +0.6 .. +27 if the loop's register moves overlap the acceptance and -27 .. +13 if they do not; the K = 1 cells, where the two bounds coincide, give w = 3.1 / 5.0 / 13.0 (b300, masks 1 / 3 / 15) and 2.7 / 3.6 / 10.7 (h100). A fence without stores costs 30.0 cycles on both devices at every K. Rule: a proxy fence of a CTA with shared stores in flight starts when they are accepted and then takes its own service latency plus storage.shared.fence.cycles; the bytes term is dropped. New leaf value = median of the three K = 1 cells: 5.0 (b300), 3.6 (h100), experimental, source shared.<device>.store_step, replacing 75.26 + bytes / 569.0 and 74.51 + bytes / 751.8 (tma_store_loaded.<device>.fence_drain). The old value over-counts a dirty fence by 70-100 cycles once the acceptance itself is charged.
